name: Colombia
gaps: Meta, Casanare, Arauca, Vichada, Guaviare, Guainía departments have few findable groups with own sites; mostly rely on national RNOA network or Global Big Day coordination.
Dropped, link dead when checked on 2026-08-09: Fondo Filantrópico ATA (Countrywide); Asociación Río Cali (Valle del Cauca)

groups.name: Asociación Calidris
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Colombia, studying and conserving birds and their habitats through research and field work across the country.

groups.name: ProAves
groups.blurb: The largest private reserve system in Colombia protecting endangered species and 68 percent of threatened birds through conservation and ecotourism.

groups.name: Red Nacional de Observadores de Aves (RNOA)
groups.blurb: National network coordinating cooperation and information exchange among regional ornithological associations and bird observers.

groups.name: Asociación Colombiana de Ornitología (ACO)
groups.blurb: Scientific society founded 2002 advancing study and conservation of Colombian birds through publication and research.

groups.name: Global Big Day Colombia
groups.blurb: Organizing committee coordinating thousands of birdwatchers across Colombia for the annual global citizen science event.

groups.name: Pajareritos
groups.blurb: Foundation introducing children to bird observation and conservation through education and guided outings.

groups.name: Guardián de las Aves
groups.blurb: Children's conservation programme connecting young people to birds and environmental protection nationwide.

groups.name: Instituto Humboldt
groups.blurb: National research institute for biological diversity and ecosystems, supporting ornithological research and conservation.

groups.name: Asociación Bogotana de Ornitología (ABO)
groups.blurb: Nonprofit dedicated to bird conservation and study in Bogotá and surrounding regions through bird walks and counts.

groups.name: Grupo Observadores de Aves Universidad Nacional (GOUN)
groups.blurb: University ornithology group promoting bird study and observation among students and researchers in Bogotá.

groups.name: Sociedad Caldense de Ornitología
groups.blurb: Founded 1984, second oldest ornithological society in Colombia, studying and defending birds in Caldas department.

groups.name: Sociedad Quindíana de Ornitología
groups.blurb: Regional ornithology society coordinating bird observation and conservation in the Coffee Triangle region.

groups.name: Sociedad Antioqueña de Ornitología (SAO)
groups.blurb: Founded 1984 with 210 members, publishing the oldest indexed ornithological journal in Colombia (SAO Bulletin).

groups.name: Sociedad Ornitológica de Córdoba (SOC)
groups.blurb: Founded 2019, discovering new species and running the Agami Heron community birding trail in coastal Caribbean.

groups.name: Fundación Ornitológica del Atlántico (ORNIAT)
groups.blurb: Founded 1998, studying Atlantic department birds and promoting bird observation through school field guides.

groups.name: Asociación Ornitológica de Boyacá (Ixobrychus)
groups.blurb: Regional ornithology association studying and conserving birds across Boyacá department.

groups.name: Fundación Ecológica Los Colibríes (FELCA)
groups.blurb: Founded 1991, protecting 12000 hectares of forest in Nariño and discovering 30 species new to science.

groups.name: Asociación Gaica
groups.blurb: Research and conservation organization working on biodiversity and ornithology in southwestern Colombia.

name: Ecuador
gaps: Regional ornithology clubs are active but most lack independent websites; coordinate through Aves y Conservación and national ornithology meetings.

groups.name: Aves y Conservación
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Ecuador since 1986, working in key biodiversity areas through conservation and research.

groups.name: Fundación Jocotoco
groups.blurb: Founded 1998 to protect the newly discovered Jocotoco Antpitta, now operating 16 reserves protecting 900 bird species.

groups.name: Comité Ecuatoriano de Registros Ornitológicos (CERO)
groups.blurb: Founded 2011 to establish the official Ecuador bird species list and publish peer reviewed records of bird sightings.

groups.name: Mindo Cloudforest Foundation
groups.blurb: Founded 2001, managing reserves in the Chocó bioregion with over 400 bird species and ecotourism activities.

name: Peru
gaps: Regional ornithology clubs operate mainly through Facebook and informal networks rather than dedicated websites. COAP has Lima and Cusco chapters but no central site.

groups.name: CORBIDI
groups.blurb: Major research organization promoting bird observation and inclusive birdwatching, maintaining Peru's bird records committee.

groups.name: Unión de Ornitólogos del Perú (UNOP)
groups.blurb: Nonprofit advancing ornithology through congresses, training, and publishing peer reviewed research on Peruvian birds.

groups.name: Club de Observadores de Aves del Perú (COAP)
groups.blurb: Nationwide network of regional birdwatching clubs with chapters in Lima, Cusco and other regions promoting citizen science.

groups.name: Grupo Aves del Perú
groups.blurb: Civil nonprofit institution dedicated to research and conservation of Peru's wild birds through community engagement.

name: Bolivia
gaps: Limited formal bird club infrastructure; most activity coordinated through national organizations. Regional bird watching groups exist informally but lack public web presence beyond Facebook.

groups.name: Asociación Armonía
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Bolivia since 1993, protecting threatened bird species through 28 strategic reserves and community work.

groups.name: Asociación Boliviana de Ornitología (ASBOR)
groups.blurb: Formed 2007, bringing together ornithologists and bird enthusiasts for research, conservation and citizen science.

groups.name: Club Ornitológico de La Paz Cóndores
groups.blurb: Local bird watching club in La Paz running field trips and coordination for the annual October Big Day event.

name: Venezuela
gaps: Website infrastructure for some organizations is limited due to country conditions; primary access through social media and Facebook pages. Many active bird watchers lack formalized club structures.

groups.name: Unión Venezolana de Ornitólogos (UVO)
groups.blurb: Founded 1980, uniting ornithologists and bird enthusiasts to promote study, research and conservation of Venezuelan birds.

groups.name: Fundación Tierra Viva
groups.blurb: Conservation foundation promoting bird observation and biodiversity knowledge through education and citizen science.

groups.name: Sociedad Conservacionista Audubon de Venezuela
groups.blurb: Founded 1970, promoting study, conservation and enjoyment of Venezuelan birds through education and citizen counts.

groups.name: Aves de Venezuela
groups.blurb: Large Facebook community of photography and bird observation enthusiasts sharing field encounters with Venezuelan bird species.
